request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "My crews" figure (`my-crew-due-total`), and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

The change is one file, `src/main/frontend/features/counters/HeaderCounters.tsx`. It works out which person the signed-in user is the same way the existing "Mine" figure does: their name or an alias, ignoring case. It then adds up the due-totals of the crews that person leads, using the same figure each crew row shows. If no person has the user's name, or that person leads no crew, the figure is blank.

If someone leads more than one crew and a person belongs to two of them, that person's due is counted once for each crew. That's how I read "the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up", and the tests don't cover this case.

No server or stored-data changes were needed, because the header already loads the crews and dues it needs, and this display-only change adds no audit records.
